proposal.reactor_type: Gas-liquid segmented-flow photoreactor: 1.0 mm ID FEP coil irradiated externally, followed immediately by a 3.0 bar(g) back-pressure regulator.
proposal.residence_time_basis: Pressure-corrected in-channel total volumetric flow at 21 C and 3.0 bar(g) BPR pressure (approximately 4.013 bar absolute). The gas-liquid segmented mixture is assumed to travel approximately as plug flow through the illuminated coil.
proposal.light_setup: A nominal 1.5 W 420 nm LED is positioned around the full illuminated FEP coil within a reflective, fan-cooled, light-tight enclosure. Maintain the coil at 21 C using forced-air cooling or a temperature-controlled plate. LED electrical power is specified; photon flux at the tubing is not provided by the batch procedure and should be measured or optimized if scale-up is needed.

streams.contents: Fmoc-L-methionine, 0.100 M (1.0 equiv), and 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole, 0.0100 M (10 mol%), prepared as one homogeneous solution.
streams.solvent: Anhydrous or dry acetonitrile, provided that both components remain fully dissolved.

streams.molar_equiv: 5.4 equiv total air per equiv substrate on a molar feed-rate basis; equivalent to approximately 1.13 equiv O2 per equiv substrate.

proposal.mixer_type: Low-dead-volume PEEK T-mixer, with the liquid entering the straight run and air entering the side arm immediately upstream of the illuminated coil.
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Keep substrate and photocatalyst premixed in one liquid feed so the catalyst concentration is fixed before irradiation. Introduce air only at the T-mixer to generate reproducible gas-liquid slugs, maximize oxygen transfer, and avoid prolonged storage of an oxygenated photochemical solution in the feed reservoir.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare S1 at 0.100 M Fmoc-L-methionine and 0.0100 M photocatalyst in acetonitrile; verify that the solution is homogeneous and does not precipitate during the planned run.
Protect the feed reservoir from ambient light until pumping.
Prime the liquid line with acetonitrile, then S1; prime the gas line with air.
Set the BPR to 3.0 bar(g), start liquid flow at 0.500 mL/min, then start air at 6.0 sccm.
Allow at least two in-channel residence times (10 min) after stable slug formation and stable pressure are observed before collecting a representative product fraction.
post_reactor_steps: Pass the outlet through the BPR into a vented, light-protected collection vessel in a fume hood; route vent gas safely and do not seal the collection vessel.
Collect only steady-state material after the startup hold-up period.
Analyze conversion and sulfoxide selectivity by an appropriate validated method, such as LC-MS and quantitative HPLC or NMR against a suitable standard.

For isolation, remove acetonitrile under reduced pressure and purify only as required by the analytical result; the batch protocol does not specify an isolation method, so no specific chromatography or crystallization condition is assumed.
chemistry_notes: The design preserves the reported 0.100 M substrate concentration, 10 mol% benzothiadiazole photocatalyst loading, air atmosphere, approximately 420 nm irradiation, 21 C operation, and nominal 5 min illuminated contact time.
At 0.500 mL/min, substrate feed is 0.0500 mmol/min and photocatalyst feed is 0.00500 mmol/min.

A 6.0 sccm air feed provides approximately 0.0557 mmol/min O2, or about 1.13 molar equivalents of O2 relative to the substrate feed rate. This is a stoichiometrically relevant oxygen supply rather than merely headspace exposure.

The batch result indicates 99% yield under its stated conditions, but identical performance in flow is not guaranteed because irradiance, oxygen transfer, and illuminated surface-area-to-volume ratio differ. Confirm conversion and avoid extending irradiation until overoxidation or substrate degradation has been assessed.
Solubility of Fmoc-L-methionine and the photocatalyst in acetonitrile at the stated concentrations is taken from the supplied batch protocol and should be reconfirmed at the intended run duration.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: A 5.0 min in-channel residence time directly matches the reported batch irradiation duration.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: This is the pressure-corrected in-channel total flow: 0.500 mL/min liquid plus 1.62 mL/min compressed air at 21 C and approximately 4.013 bar absolute.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: The batch protocol was run at 21 C; cooling is included because LED heating can otherwise raise coil temperature.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: The liquid feed retains the reported 0.100 M Fmoc-L-methionine concentration.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: A 3.0 bar(g) BPR stabilizes slug flow, prevents erratic gas expansion in the reactor, and permits a defined pressure correction for the air flow.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 10.6 mL divided by 2.12 mL/min gives 5.0 min under the stated in-channel conditions.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: This is a reference value calculated using the nominal inlet volumetric sum of 0.500 mL/min liquid plus 6.0 mL/min air at STP: 10.6/6.5 = 1.63 min. It is not the physical reactor residence time because the gas is compressed by the BPR.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: Calculated as 10.6 mL divided by the pressure-corrected in-channel flow of 2.12 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 420 nm follows the reported LED center wavelength.
reasoning_per_field.gas_flow_actual_mL_min: Calculated from 6.0 sccm using ideal-gas correction: 6.0 x (1.013/4.013) x (294.15/273.15) = approximately 1.62 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: A T-mixer is sufficient for generating alternating air-liquid segments in 1.0 mm ID tubing and has low dead volume.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: The supplied protocol specifies only nominal LED power and wavelength; the design therefore reproduces those reported settings without claiming an unmeasured photon flux.

literature_analogies: This design follows the common continuous-photochemistry practice of using transparent fluoropolymer tubing and external LED irradiation to improve light penetration relative to a larger batch vessel.

It also follows standard gas-liquid flow practice in which a BPR converts a gas feed specified at STP into a stable compressed segmented flow, improving oxygen-transfer reproducibility compared with relying on a static air headspace.
These are general engineering analogies rather than a claim that an exact published flow procedure for this specific substrate-photocatalyst pair has been validated.
safety_flags: Use a pressure-rated reactor, fittings, and BPR; verify compatibility with acetonitrile and operate behind a physical shield.
Compressed air supports oxidation. Keep the pressurized gas system free of oil, grease, incompatible elastomers, and ignition sources.
Acetonitrile is volatile, toxic, and flammable; prepare and collect material in a ventilated fume hood and use compatible waste handling.
Use a light-tight enclosure and appropriate eye/skin protection for 420 nm high-intensity LED exposure.
Install an upstream check valve on the gas line and monitor pressure continuously to prevent liquid backflow and to identify blockage or precipitation.
Do not collect into a sealed vessel downstream of the BPR because dissolved and entrained gas will disengage.
Because oxygen availability and photon flux can affect selectivity, begin with a short, monitored run and analyze for unreacted sulfide and possible overoxidation products before extended operation.
